feedback.problem: Evaluate the line integral of the function $f(x,y)=xy\sqrt{{y}^{2}+1}$ along the circle $C$ with equation ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=9.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

The curve $C$ is a circle of radius $3$ centered at $O.$ It can be parametrized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,0\le t\le 2\pi .
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡t+9{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{9({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=xy\sqrt{{y}^{2}+1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\sqrt{(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+1} \\  & =9\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡t+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }9\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡t+1}\cdot 3\cdot \text{d}t \\  & =27{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡t+1}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=9{sin}^{2}⁡t+1,$ $\text{d}u=18\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}27{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡t+1}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{1}^{1}\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(0) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
